opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Warehouse staff, checkout, and running the company.

follow100Note: Of every $100 Costco took in, $1.97 was membership fees — money that costs almost nothing to earn, which is how a warehouse retailer keeps $2.97 of profit on razor-thin store margins. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Costco's merchandise costs include buying, freight and shrink (lost or damaged goods) — the direct cost of what's on the shelves.

kpis.label: Comparable sales
kpis.note: total company, adjusted for fuel and currency

oneTimers: Results included a $72M tax benefit ($0.16 per share) related to stock-based compensation — smaller than last year's $100M benefit, so the year-ago comparison is slightly harder, not easier.
otherDetail: Interest income and other of $155M, less $35M of interest expense.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in the warehouses and online — comparable sales rose 6.4%, and digitally-enabled sales jumped 20.5%.

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual member fees — almost pure profit once collected.

takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 6.4% across the company — U.S. +5.9%, Canada +6.5%, other international +8.8% — and digitally-enabled sales jumped 20.5%.
takeaways.title: Shoppers kept coming

takeaways.text: Membership fees grew 14% to $1.33B. Costco runs its warehouses close to break-even on the goods themselves; the fees are what turn into the $2.0B bottom line.
takeaways.title: Membership is the profit engine

takeaways.text: Costco ended the quarter with 923 warehouses, including 633 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 114 in Canada and 42 in Mexico.
takeaways.title: Still expanding

verdict: Costco's sales rose 8.2% to $66.0B as comparable sales grew 6.4% — and with $1.33B of nearly cost-free membership fees on top, profit rose 11% to $2.0B.
